chunks: Draw a PLL block diagram. The question: Draw a block diagram.
A PLL block diagram is a loop of boxes with one signal going around.
The reference goes in, the output comes out, and a copy of the output (divided down) goes back to be compared with the reference.
Drawing it means putting the right boxes in the right order and labeling the signals.
Picture a one-way circular track with five stations in order: phase detector, charge pump, loop filter, VCO, and divider.
The reference clock joins at the first station, and the output is taken off right after the VCO.
Everything going around the loop is the correction signal that keeps the output in step.
The loop reads left to right through the forward path (PFD to charge pump to loop filter to VCO) and returns along the bottom through the divider.
The signals are labelled on the wires. When locked, f fb equals f ref and so f out equals Nf ref .
f ref : the reference clock frequency that enters the loop. Feedback path: the branch that carries the divided output back to the detector.
UP / DOWN pulses: the detector's outputs telling the VCO to speed up or slow down. Control voltage: ( V ctrl ): the smoothed voltage that sets the VCO's frequency.
Lock condition: f out over N equals f ref .
The smallest version has four things in words: a phase detector, a loop filter, a VCO, and a divide-by- N in the return path. The reference enters the detector.
The detector output goes through the filter into the VCO. The VCO output is the PLL output, and it is also divided by N and sent back to the detector.
With f ref equals 10 megahertz and N equals 5 , locked output is 50 megahertz. That is the whole idea.

"Left to right: reference clock into a phase-frequency detector; its UP and DOWN outputs drive a charge pump; that feeds a loop filter, an R–C network; the filter's control voltage drives the VCO, whose output is f out.
A divide-by-N block takes f out and feeds it back to the second input of the PFD, closing the loop.
I'd label f ref, UP/DOWN, the pump current, V control, f out and f out over N, and write f out equals N times f ref as the lock condition."
